items.title: Rising fuel costs force Australians to rethink Easter holidays
items.description: Rising fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict are hitting the domestic tourism sector, with cancellations surging ahead of the Easter long weekend.

items.title: Australian fears about Iran war run deeper than an anti-Trump attitude
items.description: The pandemic demonstrated that when global events become local, Australians are quick to turn on even a mighty trading partner. There is a real capacity here for the war to sour our attitude to the US alliance.

items.title: Decade-old decisions come home to roost, leaving a different oil shock
items.description: The early 2010s were the years of peak globalisation, when it seemed all trade barriers were on a one-way trip to elimination. That was before Donald Trump arrived and ruptured the global order.

items.title: Iran warns US against ground invasion as key diplomats meet in Pakistan for talks
items.description: Iran's parliament speaker says Iran is prepared to confront any American forces on its soil and would set troops "on fire" in its warning against a US ground invasion.

items.title: At the 'Gate of Tears', a new threat to global energy emerges
items.description: The opening of a new front in the Middle East war has put another vital shipping route on edge. Known in Arabic as the "Gate of Tears", analysts warn this narrow waterway could soon live up to its name.

items.title: 'Out of the pocket of taxpayers': Unis spend $1.8b on consultants and contractors
items.description: Consultancies have been accused of infiltrating universities and wasting scarce public funds on questionable advice about cutting courses and jobs.

items.title: Do you know who owns your GP clinic? The answer might surprise you
items.description: Major insurers like Medibank Private and Bupa are buying up GP clinics in a move that could lead to US-style managed care.

items.title: Bondi nanny accused of torture for Pinochet makes last stand to evade extradition
items.description: Adriana Rivas has been a fugitive in Australia since fleeing Chile while on bail 20 years ago. A federal court hearing will determine whether she is removed to face trial for the alleged crimes of torture and kidnapping, committed on behalf of the Pinochet regime.

items.title: Two jobs, no home: The 'almost hidden crisis' hurting single-parent families
items.description: Hunter was plunged into homelessness when his family lost their rental. It is an increasingly similar story to other single parents finding themselves "lifelong renters".

items.title: Liberals dump Moira Deeming from ticket for next state election
items.description: Controversial Victorian MP Moira Deeming has lost her preselection battle for the state election, with Liberal Party members replacing her with business leader Dinesh Gourisetty.

items.title: Labor wins blue-ribbon seat of Morphett from Liberals
items.description: Liberal frontbencher Stephen Patterson loses his bid to be re-elected in the beachside seat of Morphett in the South Australian state election.

items.title: No transport relief for Sydneysiders as fuel prices surge
items.description: The NSW Liberals and the Rail, Tram and Bus Union (RTBU) have renewed calls for free public transport in response to surging fuel prices.

items.title: Shane Flanagan on the challenge of coaching on after son's scary neck injury
items.description: St George Illawarra five-eighth Kyle Flanagan was transported to hospital after a head knock in the Dragons' 22-14 loss to the Gold Coast Titans.

items.title: Demons overwhelm Blues in late MCG surge
items.description: The Demons complete an amazing comeback and pile pressure on Carlton coach Michael Voss, while West Coast celebrates an inspirational victory on the road against Port Adelaide.

items.title: The best and worst things about being on reality TV, according to Guy Sebastian
items.description: Singing his way into the Australian public's hearts way back in 2003, Guy Sebastian has since had a fascinating and varied career. We catch up with the star to find out about the little things that keep him going — from his two sons to his favourite TV show.

items.title: Quiz: Can you go back in time and nail our quiz?
items.description: Cast your mind back and see if you can conquer this week's round of trivia.

items.title: You, Me & Tuscany marks the return of the romcom — and the audience is aboard
items.description: You, Me & Tuscany is highly anticipated by fans of Halle Bailey and Regé-Jean Page, who can't wait for a rare romantic comedy to hit cinemas.

items.title: Annie is only 26, but will die within months. Here's what she wants you to know
items.description: Before ending her life through voluntary assisted dying, Annaliese Holland shares her final wishes and advice on living a full life.

items.title: Quick hits: F1 driver limps from crash, teenager sets more records
items.description: Oliver Bearman limped away from a big crash after he needed to take evasive action. Here are the quick hits from the F1 Japanese Grand Prix.

items.title: How Australia is supporting NASA's first Moon flight in 50 years
items.description: Canberra-based communications systems will support NASA's first crewed lunar mission in more than half a century, helping astronauts orbit the Moon and return data.

items.title: 'It's a nightmare': Complaints pile up over Booking.com grievances
items.description: Hundreds of complaints against Booking.com are piling up as customers and hosts allege they have lost money, their property has been trashed and no-one is taking responsibility.

items.title: 'No Kings' protests against Trump draw crowds across US and Europe
items.description: Huge crowds rally against US President Donald Trump from coast to coast in what organisers hope will be the largest single-day protest in US history.

items.title: Charlie was at the airport to pick me up. We've been 'us' ever since
items.description: After cancelling a full Sri Lankan wedding and a string of "disastrous" relationships, Sashi Perera found herself opposite a man who made believing in him simple.

items.title: 'A lover of life': Mal Leyland eyes off one final trip before dementia decline
items.description: Adventurer and filmmaker Mal Leyland, of Ask the Leyland Brothers fame, shares his private health battle. But the TV legend is determined to retrace the cross-country trip that made him famous 60 years ago.

items.title: Why the 'perfect pair' of jeans remains an elusive concept
items.description: The enduring challenge of finding the "perfect pair" of jeans highlights the garment's cultural significance, and the opportunity to move toward more sustainable and more thoughtfully designed denim.
